### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx`  _(via EmailTemplateDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7b172babc34cab4dd805af9ce09ebc9969f27165` — the merge of head `49258decf331b8a12c16270a505d99bf68ab5b27` into base `912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7b172babc34cab4dd805af9ce09ebc9969f27165 && git checkout 7b172babc34cab4dd805af9ce09ebc9969f27165
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0 49258decf331b8a12c16270a505d99bf68ab5b27 && git checkout -B drift-repro 912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0 && git merge --no-ff 49258decf331b8a12c16270a505d99bf68ab5b27

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 912076f8854b96093e11480f369456100f2de3d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `511e09b12f88b60f995cb0483a1b27c0d4b68339`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/mail-hole-grammar.ts, packages/formula/src/template-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/template-currency-code-path.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-email-template-hole-grammar.currency-path.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.email-template-writes.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-currency-code-path.render.test.ts + packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-action-copy-templates.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts, ui/packages/core/src/actions/actionCopyTemplate.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow-text-slot-template.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/action-copy-template.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/bulk-action.zod.ts, docs/adr/0032-unified-expression-layer.md, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx

Face: the file list carries a published schema (`packages/spec/src/system/email-template.zod.ts`) and a governed path (`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`, Tier H), so the record is at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on the schema face; the floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces, and the `skills/**` hunk is reviewed sentence by sentence against the code. Inputs: card #26660 (body and every comment: triage `6441491903`, the server seat's claim `6445327635`, reports `6447779926` / `6449628305` / `6450298695`, amendment `6447835110`, ACCEPT `6450367555`, release `6451239827`, retriage `6452088840`, the spec seat's claim `6452747733`, the dev's report `6455019677`); PR #26799 (merged, `dabe77182`) and its contract review `6450017524`; PR #26937's body, file list, the one bot comment, and the net diff against `main` at the head (18 files, +779 / −50, two commits on the merge-base `5ce3404a`: `d1fffa10` the feature, `511e09b1` a merge of `origin/main`); the check-runs on `511e09b12` read four times (the readings are declared in ③). `.changeset/*` and `content/docs/**` read sentence by sentence, not reviewed as code. Local repository reads were `git show` / `git grep` on a ref fetched for this review; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each named RIGHT or WRONG against the tree at the head.

1. **`email_template` `subject` / `bodyText` / `bodyHtml` admit `currency:@path`** — `@`, then a dotted path of word characters with no empty segment, unquoted, nothing between the mark and the path. **Unambiguous against the literal for every input:** the literal is `CURRENCY_CODE_RE = /^[A-Z]{3}$/` (`template-engine.ts:191`) and the path form is `CURRENCY_CODE_PATH_RE = /^@(\w+(?:\.\w+)*)$/` (`:217`); the first can never match a string that begins with `@`, the second can never match one that does not, so the two accept sets are disjoint and no third shape is admitted (`currency:currency_code`, `currency:record.currency_code`, `currency:eur`, `currency:`, `currency:'@x'`, `currency:@`, `currency:@ x`, `currency:@a..b` all stay `currency-code-literal`). The mail parser's `FILTER_RE` (`mail-hole-grammar.ts:57`) hands `@currency_code` as `arg`; the judge (`template-engine.ts:312-315`) tests `isCurrencyCode(arg)` first, then `currencyCodePath(formatterPart)` on the raw text, so quotes defeat the mark (`currency:'@x'` is refused) and `currency: @x` (space after the colon, which `FILTER_RE` and `currencyCodePath` both trim) is admitted in both readers alike. **The rule is one sentence, said one way:** `CURRENCY_ARGUMENT_RULE` (`template-engine.ts:178-181`) is quoted verbatim by the spec's `MAIL_TEMPLATE_HOLES` (`email-template.zod.ts:107-111`, pinned word for word against the built spec in `template-currency-code-path.test.ts:487-490`), by the lint hint (`validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:90-91`), and by every refusal sentence the renderer can throw (`currencyArgumentRefusal` mail arm `:200-207`, `currencyCodeValueRefusal` `:256-264`, `currency-code-path-undeclared` `mail-hole-grammar.ts:155-159`). RIGHT.

2. **The `@path` is resolved against the mail template's own data roots, exactly as a `{{ path }}` hole is.** `plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts:137` resolves `parsed.codePath` with the same `lookup(data, …)` that `:130` resolves `parsed.path` with, over the same `data` (`defaultTemplateContext` spread under `input.data`, `email-service.ts:1418-1421`), with the same dotted-path semantics (`lookup` `:62-71`). All three faces go through the one `render` function (`renderTemplate` / `renderPlainTextTemplate` `:93-114`; `email-service.ts:1474-1478`), double- or triple-braced (the mail pattern's group 2 is the inner body either way). No root-spelled argument (`record.`) exists in mail, and the bare path stays refused, so nothing but the send's data can be read. RIGHT.

3. **One grammar: every in-app dialect refuses the marked form at save, by name.** `judgeHoleFormatter`'s fifth argument defaults to `'in-app'` (`template-engine.ts:300`); only `mail-hole-grammar.ts:95,100` pass `'mail'`. The in-app `parseHole` (`:418`) passes no dialect, so `currency:@record.currency_code` yields `currency-code-path-mail-only` (`:316-326`), `compileTemplate` answers `kind: 'parse'` (`:449-451`), and `validate.ts:963` turns that into `invalid-template`. Every save door of the in-app dialect reaches that compile: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:2804` (flow text slots) and `:3554`, `validate-action-copy-templates.ts:129` (action and bulk-action `confirmText` / `successMessage`), `service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts:619` (`registerFlow`); the two runtime evaluators, `service-automation/src/builtin/template.ts:122` and `ui/packages/core/src/actions/actionCopyTemplate.ts:93`, call `templateEngine.evaluate`, which compiles first (`:474-475`) — no dialect reaches `FORMATTERS.currency` with an `@` argument. The three in-app describes (`flow-text-slot-template.ts:21-23`, `action-copy-template.ts:162-186`, `bulk-action.zod.ts:470`) spell `formatter[:arg]` and `currency:EUR` and say nothing of a path, so they stay true unchanged; `titleFormat` and `promptTemplate` ride the same engine. RIGHT.

4. **Never a silent default currency for the new form.** In the renderer (`plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts:136-141`) the code is read and judged by `currencyCodeValueRefusal` BEFORE the amount is formatted; a refusal throws `TEMPLATE_INVALID` and `formatValue` is never reached, so a `codePath` hole can never hand `formatValue` an `undefined` argument (`:140` assigns the judged code), which is the only way the `'USD'` default at `template-engine.ts:84` is reached. `currencyCodeValueRefusal` admits only a string matching `/^[A-Z]{3}$/` as stored (no trim), so missing, `null`, `eur`, `' EUR'`, a number and an object are all refused, each named with the hole, the path and the value (`describeCodeValue`); the `email-service.ts:1479-1486` wrap prefixes `email template NAME (locale=L)` and rethrows every non-`TEMPLATE_INVALID` error unchanged. A null amount with a missing code is still refused (the code is judged first). `formatValue('currency', …)` itself still throws `RangeError` for a non-code argument (`:79-81`) and never reads a path. No `USD` appears anywhere on the new path. The #26799 pin files (`template-hole-grammar.test.ts`, `template-hole-grammar.render.test.ts`, `validate-email-template-hole-grammar.test.ts`, the door test's existing cases) are absent from the file list, so they are unchanged; their green is Test Core's verdict in ③. RIGHT.

5. **Save time: an undeclared `@path` is refused when the template declares variables; accepted when it declares none.** `judgeMailHoleGrammar(face, { variables })` (`mail-hole-grammar.ts:141-165`) refuses `currency-code-path-undeclared` only when `variables.length > 0` and no declared name equals the path or is a root it lies under (`isDeclaredPath` `:116-118`). The lint rule passes `declaredVariableNames(template.variables)` (`validate-email-template-hole-grammar.ts:65-70`, a malformed entry declares nothing); the publish door reaches it through `runtime-gate.ts:190` (`email_template → emailTemplates`), `422 INVALID_METADATA` pinned on `code`, `status` and `issues` in the metadata-protocol test. With no variables the path is judged at render (item 4). **Honest in the describe:** `variables[].name` says "When the template declares any variable, the path of a `currency:@path` argument must be one of them or lie under one" (`email-template.zod.ts:114-117`); the lint changeset, the docs page (`email-templates.mdx:115-117`) and `MailHoleGrammarOptions` say the same with the no-variables case spelled out. It is also consistent with how a hole's own `{{ path }}` is treated today: no door judges a hole path against `variables` either; only `required` ones are enforced, at render (`requireVars`). RIGHT.

6. **Tests, read against the floor:** formula (38) — 3 accepted and 10 refused path shapes, mail parse carrying `codePath`, malformed marks refused as `currency-code-literal` quoting the rule, declared/undeclared/root/none-declared/literal-not-judged, value refusals for six shapes, in-app compile + `validateExpression` + evaluate refusing by name, `formatValue` throwing on the unresolved mark, and the spec-describe parity pin; plugin-email (12) — one bundle with `en-US` and `zh-CN` rows, `EUR` and `CNY` records formatted in every face (`€1,234.50` / `CN¥1,234.50` / `¥1,234.50`), `sendTemplate` delivering two records in their own currencies, three refusals in both locales asserting the `TEMPLATE_INVALID: email template contract.overdue (locale=L)` prefix, the hole, the value, no `$` / `US$` / `USD 1` in the message and nothing sent, the html face judged on its own path, the literal form and the bare-path refusal unchanged; lint (13) — accept with no variables and with the path or its root declared, refuse per face, malformed marks, hint quoting the rule, every `os` command, the runtime publish gate; metadata-protocol (+1) — the door's `code` + `status` + `issues`, plus the declared and the no-variables admits. Two currencies, two locales, refusals with `code` asserted and no USD: present. RIGHT.

7. **Public surface (additive):** `@objectstack/formula` exports `CURRENCY_ARGUMENT_RULE`, `currencyCodePath`, `currencyCodeValueRefusal`, types `TemplateHoleDialect`, `MailHoleGrammarOptions`; `judgeHoleFormatter` gains an optional fifth parameter; `TemplateHoleGrammarRule` gains two members; `ParsedMailHole` gains `codePath`; `judgeMailHoleGrammar` gains an optional options argument. No removal, no rename. RIGHT.

Should-fix (level unaffected, no sentence this PR publishes is false):

- **S1** — `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:2458-2463`, the comment above the rule's registry row, still reads "a `currency` argument that is not a literal ISO 4217 code is refused, naming the literal-only rule". The diff leaves it; it is now incomplete (the marked path is admitted; a fourth rule exists). A source comment, not a runtime string — fix in the next touch of that file or a follow-up.
- **S2** — the new `MAIL_TEMPLATE_HOLES` describe says "with one formatter from the template engine whitelist per hole". The one-formatter half is refused (`one-formatter`); the whitelist half is not: `judgeHoleFormatter` never checks `TEMPLATE_FORMATTERS`, and the renderer prints the raw value for an unknown formatter (`plugin-email/src/template-engine.ts:150`, "unknown formatter → raw"). Pre-existing and declared unchanged in #26799's review (① item 7); this PR is the first to state the whitelist in a published `.describe()`. As a grammar statement it is true; as a promise of refusal it is not made. Either refuse an unknown mail formatter at save (a narrowing, its own card) or soften the clause to "an optional formatter". Carrier: the seat; not this PR's defect.

### ② Semver level

Four changesets, read against what the diff publishes:

- `@objectstack/formula` **minor** — `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. RIGHT: a form every door refused until now is accepted in the mail dialect, in a hole grammar the contract review on #26799 read as spec-documented and the retriage (`6452088840`) ruled a protocol addition; new exports ride the same level. The in-app dialect's `currency-code-path-mail-only` refuses a form it already refused (as `currency-code-literal`), so nothing narrows.
- `@objectstack/plugin-email` **minor** — `yes` / `added`. RIGHT (a stored value the renderer now renders; the new refusals are all on the new form).
- `@objectstack/lint` **minor** — `yes` / `added`. RIGHT; `currency-code-path-undeclared` refuses only a form that was never accepted, so `added` stands, not `narrowed`.
- `@objectstack/spec` **minor** — `yes` / `added`, descriptions only. RIGHT by the retriage's own reading: the `email_template` face describes are where the protocol states its hole grammar, and the regenerated reference (`content/docs/references/system/email-template.mdx`) carries the sentence to readers. No Zod shape, default or key moves (`z.string()` unchanged), so a reader could argue `none` / `patch`; `added` follows the ruling that item (b) is a `domain:spec` protocol addition and is the conservative level. Not a finding.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: a test only, no changeset. RIGHT. `Check Changeset` success on the head.
- **ADR-0087: not-required** with its reason — RIGHT: a `Clause-②: yes` changeset with no `(narrowing)` arm owes no disposition marker (`check-adr-0087-registration` reads the arm), and the reason holds: the marked form was refused at save and at render before, so no stored template or built artifact carries it and every form accepted before renders as before. ADR-0032 §3 read (`docs/adr/0032-unified-expression-layer.md:76-80`): holes are paths plus a whitelisted formatter, never logic; the ADR fixes no shape for a formatter's argument, and `@path` is a path, not logic, so no ADR amendment is owed and no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry names these files.
- PR body carries `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, both matching the claim `6452747733` and all four changesets.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag, deviation and `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

- **`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md:448-450` (Tier H), sentence by sentence.** "A `currency` argument is a literal code (`currency:EUR`)" — true: the in-app dialect admits only `/^[A-Z]{3}$/` (`template-engine.ts:312-326`), and the literal form is the mail dialect's default too. "only an email template may read it from the send's data instead, `{{ amount | currency:@currency_code }}`" — true: `'mail'` is passed only at `mail-hole-grammar.ts:95,100`, the in-app judge refuses the form as `currency-code-path-mail-only`, and the example is the accepted shape. The sentence sits under the `template` dialect row whose carriers name `system/email-template` `subject` / `bodyHtml` / `bodyText` (`:444`), so "email template" names a carrier the reader has just seen. The paragraph's existing sentences ("Missing template paths render as the empty string", "a template holds a path and a formatter, nothing else") stay true. **Token ceiling:** the file at the head is 22692 bytes; minus the 20-byte `version:` line, ceil(22672 / 4) = 5668 against the `CEILINGS` row 5997 (`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs:444`); `main` reads 5627 (22527 bytes); the gate and `check:skill-docs` / `check:skill-refs` run in `Type Check · source gates`, success on the head. 471 → 473 lines; no other file mirrors the sentence; no other skill teaches the `currency` hole formatter (every other `currency` in `skills/` is the field type or a dashboard measure). **Docs:** `content/docs/automation/email-templates.mdx:91-121` read sentence by sentence against items 1-5 and the plugin-email test's outputs — each true; "`currency` with no argument formats in US dollars" is `template-engine.ts:84`. The in-app pages that teach a no-argument `| currency` (`flows.mdx:472`, `:2332`; `formulas.mdx:79`) stay true. The four CLI transcripts #26799 touched carry rule counts only and name no currency rule.
- **Dev question 1 — `currency` with no argument still formats in USD.** No sentence this PR publishes is made false by leaving it: the docs page, the formula and plugin-email changesets and the `FORMATTERS` comment all say no argument formats in US dollars, and item 4 shows the new form can never reach that default. Triage's "⛔ never a silent default currency" (`6441491903`) was written about a PATH argument substituting USD; the retriage graded item (b) and did not re-grade the no-argument default; the release `6451239827` carried it so it is not lost. Judged: correct to leave out of this PR — a `(narrowing)` arm would change this PR's face and its migration note. The dev's recommendation A (a separate narrowing card, prescription `currency:USD` or in mail `currency:@path`, one-line D3 note, migrating the 2 docs, 4 describes and 4 pins the census names) is sound; the seat files it. Escalation: the seat's card, not this record's FAIL.
- **Dev question 2 — the eval owed in `skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json`.** The PR's `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json` is the claim grammar's own form (pm-dispatch `SKILL.md:313`: `updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON`; `updated here` requires the evals to exercise it). Its absence is a missing sentence, not a false one: nothing in the PR claims an eval exercises `currency:@path`. The checklist (`review-checklist.md:18`) requires the seat to file the card and rewrite `owed — FILES` to `#N` before ACCEPT; the eval text the dev proposes (ask for an `email_template` showing an overdue amount in each contract's own currency; expect `{{ amount | currency:@currency_code }}`, a code in capitals, the path declared when the template declares `variables`) matches items 1, 4 and 5. Escalation: the seat files it; a Tier H surface, so its own PR needs its own approval.
- **Deviation: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.email-template-writes.test.ts` beyond the claim's named files** — test only, no changeset, the publish-door host pin the order's "lint / publish-door tests" asks for, beside #26799's cases in the same file. Answered.
- **Deviation: branch `claude/project-thread-wonj87`, not `claude/issue-26660-*`** — the claim `6452747733` states it as measured; `Implemented-by` below carries it. Answered.
- **Deviation: one merge of `origin/main` (`511e09b1`)** — the net diff against `main` at the head is the same 18 files as the API diff; no `main` content rides in under the PR's name. Answered.
- **Deviations: reviewer request not made; PR activity not subscribed** — procedural, outside this record. Noted.
- **Attribution:** both commits end with the model-free trailer pair (`Claude-Session`, `Co-authored-by: Claude`); the PR body carries the AGENTS.md session-URL footer and, above it, the harness's emoji footer — two footers, no model identifier. Wording only.
- **In-app reading of a code from data is not built** — noted in the acceptance notes, refused by name (item 3), no defect. Answered.
- **Governance:** `skills/**` in the file list makes the whole PR Tier H; draft; head repo is the base repo; 779 + 50 changed lines; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success. No AI seat merges, queues, arms auto-merge or readies this PR; the maintainer's approval (`GOVERNED_APPROVERS`) lifts it and the owning seat lands it. This record is a review of record, ⛔ not that approval.
- **Check-runs on `511e09b12`** (`/commits/{sha}/check-runs`): read at 2026-10-27T22:24:43Z and 2026-10-27T22:28:22Z, the gate-carrying `Test Core (1/8 … 8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace` and `Type Check UI` were `in_progress` — an honest reading, not a pass; polled once a minute after that. Final reading at 2026-10-27T22:39:49Z, 47 rows, none pending: every one of the eight required contexts concluded `success` — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and its eight shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`; `Lint UI` skipped by its path selector. Advisory contexts: `Check Changeset`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test UI`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter` — all success; `Lint UI`, the dogfood and `Test UI` shards, `Temporal Conformance`, the upgrade harness and the tarball smoke — skipped by selector or opt-in.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
